questions.question: Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Dad: “Yes, tell me.” B. Laxmi: “Dad, I need to speak to you.” C. Dad: “I think you are still too young for it.” D. Laxmi: “Please buy me a scooter.”
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Dad: “Yes, tell me.”

B. Laxmi: “Dad, I need to speak to you.”

C. Dad: “I think you are still too young for it.”

D. Laxmi: “Please buy me a scooter.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BADC.'

Key Points

  • The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "a necessity or obligation by Laxmi to speak to her Dad". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
  • Sentence A will come after B as it is talking about Laxmi's Dad allowing her to speak.
  • Sentence D will come after A as it is giving information about Laxmi's polite request to her Dad for a scooter.
  • The sentence 'C' is the concluding part because it is talking about Dad's thoughts on whether to buy a scooter for Laxmi or not.
     

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: Laxmi: “Dad, I need to speak to you.” Dad: “Yes, tell me.” Laxmi: “Please buy me a scooter.” Dad: “I think you are still too young for it.”

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
       

Hinglish

  • वाक्य 'B' किसी अन्य वाक्य से स्वतंत्र है क्योंकि यह "लक्ष्मी द्वारा अपने पिता से बात करने की आवश्यकता या दायित्व" के बारे में सामान्य जानकारी दे रहा है। अतः 'B' पहला भाग है।
  • वाक्य A, B के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह लक्ष्मी के पिता द्वारा उसे बोलने की अनुमति देने की बात कर रहा है।
  • वाक्य D, A के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह लक्ष्मी के अपने पिता को स्कूटर के लिए विनम्र अनुरोध के बारे में जानकारी दे रहा है।
  • वाक्य 'C' अंतिम भाग है क्योंकि यह पिताजी के विचारों के बारे में बात कर रहा है कि लक्ष्मी के लिए स्कूटर खरीदना है या नहीं।

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) willing to go Q) is not R) my son S) camping
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
P) willing to go
Q) is not
R) my son
S) camping
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (1) i.e. RQPS
Key Points
  • The sentence starts with part (R), "my son," which is the subject of the sentence.
  • Next, part (Q) adds the main verb, saying "is not," which negates the action.
  • Part (P) continues by introducing the action, "willing to go," indicating the condition of the subject.
  • Finally, part (S) concludes with the activity, "camping," specifying the activity that my son is not willing to do.
Therefore, the correct answer is RQPS.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2 (SPRQ): This option disrupts the natural sequence by placing "willing to go" after the verb.
  • Option 3 (PQRS): This option lacks logical flow and wrong sequence as it misses the intended meaning.
  • Option 4 (QRSP): This option begins with a negation that creates an incomplete and awkward structure.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) her face Q) I have R) for a year S) not seen

P) her face
Q) I have
R) for a year
S) not seen
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (4) i.e. QSPR
Key Points
  • The sentence begins with the subject "I have," which is correctly indicated by part (Q).
  • Following the subject, "not seen" (S) continues the logical sequence, making it clear what the subject has not done.
  • The next part, "her face," (P) provides the object that the subject has not seen.
  • Ending with, "for a year" (R) completes the sentence by stating the duration.
Therefore, the correct answer is QSPR.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (PQRS): This option starts with "her face I have not seen for a year," which disrupts the logical flow and structure of the sentence.
  • Option 2 (PSQR): This option starts with "her face not seen I have for a year," which creates an incorrect and confusing structure.
  • Option 3 (SPQR): This option starts with "not seen her face I have for a year," which is awkward and grammatically incorrect.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. Birds’ heart, lungs and P. uptake and intensive exertion compared Q. to humans, which enables them to function R. efficiently at these very high altitudes S. muscles are more efficient for oxygen
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Birds’ heart, lungs and

P. uptake and intensive exertion compared

Q. to humans, which enables them to function

R. efficiently at these very high altitudes

S. muscles are more efficient for oxygen
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. "SPQR." 
 Key Points 

  • In the abovementioned paragraph, there is a chronological sequence of the sentences.
  • Sentence S is the first part of the sentence as it begins with the 'Birds’ heart, lungs and' so we have to use a word related to birds body which is 'muscles.' The sentence starts with the topic of discussion - the efficiency of birds' heart, lungs, and muscles in high-altitude environments. It states that birds' muscles are more efficient for oxygen uptake.
  • Sentence P is the second part of the sentence as it begins with 'uptake and intensive exertion' and then continues by stating that birds' muscles are more efficient for oxygen uptake and intensive exertion compared to humans. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
  • The only option that shows such an arrangement is Option 3.
  • Sentence Q is the third part of the sentence as it raises the question that what is the function of the efficiency of oxygen uptake and intensive exertion. Thus it builds a relationship with the previous and upcoming parts.

  • Sentence R is the last part of the sentence as it concludes by stating the answer to the previous question that this efficiency is what enables birds to function efficiently at these very high altitudes, emphasizing the significance of their unique physiological adaptations.

  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

The correct order is: 

Birds’ heart, lungs and

S. muscles are more efficient for oxygen

P. uptake and intensive exertion compared

Q. to humans, which enables them to function

R. efficiently at these very high altitudes

questions.question: Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) that further treatment (B) useless (C) the doctor concluded (D) would be
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) that further treatment

(B) useless

(C) the doctor concluded

(D) would be
questions.solution: The sentence follows the subject-verb-Object (SVO) structure. "The doctor" is the subject, and "concluded" is the verb. So the first part must be C. "That further treatment" is the first part of the object. So, it must be A. The phrase "that further treatment" serves as a subordinating conjunction, connecting the doctor's conclusion to the statement about uselessness. The word "useless" is an adjective modifying the noun "treatment." So the last part must be the pair DB. Correct sentence: The doctor concluded that further treatment would be useless.

questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A) based on the

B) we live in

C) nation that

D) our nationality is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "D, A, C, B."

 Key Points

  • The sentence is talking about the relationship between our nationality and the nation we live in.
  • The sentence should start with the subject, which is "Our nationality" in this case.
  • So, the first part is D.
  • The next part should be the verb + preposition, which is "based on."
  • So, the next part is A.
  • Then, we need to add the object, which is "nation that we live in."
  • So, the next pair must be CB.
  • The sentence is in the present tense in the passive voice.
  • The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object + Prepositional Phrase.
  • The correct answer is Option 2.
     

Correct sentence: Our nationality is based on the nation that we live in.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. So I am not very sure B. I have a driving license C. Of myself reaching home safely D. But no real driving experience
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. So I am not very sure
B. I have a driving license
C. Of myself reaching home safely
D. But no real driving experience
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (3) i.e. BDAC
Key Points
  • The sentence begins with the subject "I have a driving license," which is correctly indicated by part (B). 
  • Following the subject, "but no real driving experience," (BD) continues the logical sequence, making it clear that despite having a license, there is no experience.
  • The next part, "so I am not very sure," starts the explanation about the uncertainty, indicated by (A).
  • Ending with "of myself reaching home safely" (C) completes the sentence by stating the concern about reaching home safely.
Therefore, the correct answer is BDAC.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (BCAD): This option starts with "I have a driving license of myself reaching home safely," which makes the sentence incomplete and does not make sense logically.
  • Option 2 (BDCA): This option starts with "I have a driving license but no real driving experience of myself reaching home safely," which makes the sentence incorrect as the explanation of uncertainty is missing.
  • Option 4 (CABD): This option starts with "of myself reaching home safely so I am not very sure I have a driving license," which creates a fragmented and confusing sentence structure.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. I saw a middle-aged man sitting beneath the tree with his knees drawn up to his chest. B. When I was a street away from my house, I saw a huge banyan tree to my right. C. My heart went out to him as he was crying bitterly. D. His head was bowed and his body was shivering continuously.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order.

A. I saw a middle-aged man sitting beneath the tree with his knees drawn up to his chest.

B. When I was a street away from my house, I saw a huge banyan tree to my right.

C. My heart went out to him as he was crying bitterly.

D. His head was bowed and his body was shivering continuously.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BADC'.
Key Points
  • Whenever we try to arrange the sequence of the jumbled sentences, it's important to find out the first sentence.
  • The sentence 'B' is the first one as it explains the situation perfectly. (When I was a street away from my house, I saw a huge banyan tree to my right.)
  • The second in the sequence would be the sentence 'A' that states what I saw beneath the tree. (I saw a middle-aged man sitting beneath the tree with his knees drawn up to his chest.)
  • The third in the sequence would be the sentence 'D' that tells about the condition of that middle-aged man. (His head was bowed and his body was shivering continuously.)
  • The sentence 'C' is the last one as it talks about how I felt at the end. ( My heart went out to him as he was crying bitterly.)
​Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
Additional Information
  • Let's understand some important words given in the sentences.
  • Shiver (verb) - to shake slightly or quickly because of feeling cold, ill, or frightened - She was shivering with the cold that's why she covered herself with the blanket.
  • Bitterly (adverb) - in a way that shows deep anger and pain - He was bitterly disappointed when he couldn't get through the exam.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It is unquestionably evident that this virus brought misery and grief into the lives of people of other professions too. B. Covid-19 changed the form and face of every field in the world. It did not leave any field untouched. C. One of the most affected areas is education. Millions of students all over the world could not get a proper education. D. Millions of teachers who are working, specifically in private educational institutes, were not paid a full salary during the pandemic.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It is unquestionably evident that this virus brought misery and grief into the lives of people of other professions too.

B. Covid-19 changed the form and face of every field in the world. It did not leave any field untouched.

C. One of the most affected areas is education. Millions of students all over the world could not get a proper education.

D. Millions of teachers who are working, specifically in private educational institutes, were not paid a full salary during the pandemic.
questions.solution: The first sentence explains that Covid-19 has impacted every field in the world. The second sentence highlights that education is one of the most affected areas, with millions of students not receiving proper education. The third sentence describes the plight of millions of teachers who were not paid in full during the pandemic. The last sentence shows that the virus brought misery and grief to people in other professions too. Hence, the correct order is BCDA.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. P. on the US naval base, close to the prison compounds Q. housing the remaining 39 detainees held in the “war on terror” R. inviting tenders for private contractors to run the Migrant Operations Center S. the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) bureau is
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

P. on the US naval base, close to the prison compounds

Q. housing the remaining 39 detainees held in the “war on terror”

R. inviting tenders for private contractors to run the Migrant Operations Center

S. the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) bureau is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4'.

Key Points

  • The correct order of the sentence parts is SRPQ.
  • S. the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) bureau is
    • This part introduces the subject and is the natural starting point of the sentence, as it describes who is doing the action.
  • R. inviting tenders for private contractors to run the Migrant Operations Center
    • This part provides the main action of the sentence, explaining what the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) bureau is doing.
  • P. on the US naval base, close to the prison compounds
    • This part provides further detail on the location where the Migrant Operations Center is to be run.
  • Q. housing the remaining 39 detainees held in the “war on terror”
    • Finally, this part of the sentence provides additional information related to the location mentioned in part P and helps to complete the narrative.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: "The Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) bureau is inviting tenders for private contractors to run the Migrant Operations Center on the US naval base, close to the prison compounds housing the remaining 39 detainees held in the “war on terror.”

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. Corruption is P. misuse and abuse of public office, either directly Q. typified by dishonesty, exploitation or the R. or indirectly, for personal gains or unjust enrichment S. in negation of due process or established protocol
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Corruption is

P. misuse and abuse of public office, either directly

Q. typified by dishonesty, exploitation or the

R. or indirectly, for personal gains or unjust enrichment

S. in negation of due process or established protocol
questions.solution:
The correct answer is indeed 1) QPRS.

Key Points

  • Here is the correct order of the parts of the sentence:
  • Q. typified by dishonesty, exploitation or the: This part introduces the concept of corruption and highlights its key characteristics, which include dishonesty and exploitation.
  • P. misuse and abuse of public office, either directly: This part provides further elaboration on corruption by specifying that it involves the misuse and abuse of public office. It emphasizes that corruption can occur directly within the public office itself.
  • R. or indirectly, for personal gains or unjust enrichment: This part expands on the previous point by explaining that corruption can also occur indirectly, with individuals seeking personal gains or unjust enrichment through their actions. It highlights the motive behind corrupt practices.
  • S. in negation of due process or established protocol: This part adds an important aspect of corruption, stating that it goes against due process or established protocols. It implies that corruption disregards legal and ethical procedures.
  • When rearranged, the sentence reads:
    • Corruption is typified by dishonesty, exploitation or the misuse and abuse of public office, either directly or indirectly, for personal gains or unjust enrichment, in negation of due process or established protocol.
  • This arrangement presents a coherent and logical flow of the sentence, providing a definition of corruption and describing its characteristics and consequences.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (a) the Industrial Revolution denotes (b) and continued until the middle of the 19th century (c) a significant period of social, economic and technological revolution (d) that commenced in the latter part of the 18th century
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(a) the Industrial Revolution denotes

(b) and continued until the middle of the 19th century

(c) a significant period of social, economic and technological revolution

(d) that commenced in the latter part of the 18th century
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • Part (a) comes first as it introduces the subject, "the Industrial Revolution denotes":
    • "the Industrial Revolution denotes"
  • Part (c) follows to describe what the Industrial Revolution denotes, "a significant period of social, economic and technological revolution":
    • "a significant period of social, economic and technological revolution"
  • Part (d) follows to describe the commencement time, "that commenced in the latter part of the 18th century":
    • "that commenced in the latter part of the 18th century"
  • Part (b) comes last to indicate the continuation period, "and continued until the middle of the 19th century":
    • "and continued until the middle of the 19th century"
  • The correct sequence is acdb.
 
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"The Industrial Revolution denotes a significant period of social, economic and technological revolution that commenced in the latter part of the 18th century and continued until the middle of the 19th century."

P. time and money into understanding its

Key Points

    • P. time and money into understanding its

    • R. promotions work, and changing product ingredients to

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. He drove his P: slimy road to Q: reach Shimla R: car through
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

He drove his

P: slimy road to

Q: reach Shimla 

R: car through
questions.solution:
Correct option - 3

Clearly, a sentence does not end with a preposition. Hence, options 1 & 2 are eliminated. A preposition is used before a noun but not a verb. Thus, the sequence RQ i.e. through reach is grammatically incorrect. Hence, option 4 is also eliminated. Thus, option 3 i.e. RPQ is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - He drove his car through slimy road to reach Shimla.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Inspector: “Were you sleeping when the robbers entered the bank?” B. Guard: “The iron grill lock was broken and the bank looked ransacked but the robbers could not take away anything as I had returned quickly.” C. Inspector: “What did you see when you came back?” D. Guard: “No Sir. The bank had closed and | had just gone to relieve myself.”
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Inspector: “Were you sleeping when the robbers entered the bank?”

B. Guard: “The iron grill lock was broken and the bank looked ransacked but the robbers could not take away anything as I had returned quickly.”

C. Inspector: “What did you see when you came back?”

D. Guard: “No Sir. The bank had closed and | had just gone to relieve myself.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e., 'ADCB'.

Key Points

  • When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly. 
  • The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 
  • Here, only A is independent and introduces the questioning by the Inspector. 
  • It should be followed by D which provides the guard's answer to the question asked by the Inspector.
  • So, D must come after A. Then AD is the correct order.
  • This order is shown in option 4, which shows the full sequence as: ADCB.
  • Thus, the correct sequence is: ADCB

A. Inspector: “Were you sleeping when the robbers entered the bank?”

D. Guard: “No Sir. The bank had closed and | had just gone to relieve myself.”

C. Inspector: “What did you see when you came back?”

B. Guard: “The iron grill lock was broken and the bank looked ransacked but the robbers could not take away anything as I had returned quickly.”

questions.question: Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A) about all his B) noise they make C) he constantly complains D) neighbours and the

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A) have to deal with B) about the terrible traffic C) on his way to work D) Nishit begins thinking E) he will surely
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A) have to deal with

B) about the terrible traffic

C) on his way to work

D) Nishit begins thinking

questions.solution:

  • Part B: The next logical step is to provide information about what Nishit is thinking about. In this case, it's the terrible traffic.
  • Part E: Following his thoughts about the traffic, the sentence continues to explain what Nishit is considering or planning. In this case, he is thinking about what he will surely do.

  • Part C: Finally, the sentence concludes by providing the context of when and where Nishit will have to deal with the terrible traffic.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Cheetahs are one of the world's most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed. B. Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears. C. Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly. D. They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65-85 cm [2-3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Cheetahs are one of the world's most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed.

B. Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears.

C. Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly.

D. They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65-85 cm [2-3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ABDC'.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
  • Here, 'Sentence A' should be the first sentence because the given paragraph is talking about the Cheetas. And Sentence A is an introductory sentence.
  • Sentence B will be the next sentence. (Moreover, only option 1 starts with 'A', therefore we can instantly mark it as the correct answer)
  • Sentence B is talking about the physical appearance of 'Cheetahs' and Sentence D is also talking about the physical appearance. Hence, both of these sentences are connected.
  • Hence, sentence D will be the next sentence.
  • Lastly, Sentence C will be used.
  • Thus, the correct sequence is:
    • A: Cheetahs are one of the world's most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed.
    • B: Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears.
    • D: They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65-85 cm [2-3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft.
    • C: Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly.
       

Correct Sequence: Cheetahs are one of the world's most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed. Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears. They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65-85 cm [2-3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft. Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe. B. The country has 100 major oil and gas fields. C. The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum. D. The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.
A. These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe.
B. The country has 100 major oil and gas fields.
C. The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum.
D. The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (3) i.e. CBAD
Key Points
  • The sequence begins with the introduction of the main topic, "The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum," which is correctly indicated by part (C). 
  • Following the introduction, "The country has 100 major oil and gas fields" provides further detail about the petroleum economy, indicated by (B).
  • The next part, "These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe," connects to the previous sentence by referring to the oil and gas fields, indicated by (A).
  • The final part, "The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource," gives a specific example of one of these fields, indicated by (D).
Therefore, the correct answer is CBAD.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (DCAB): This arrangement starts with the specific detail of Ghawar Field, making it less logical as an introduction to the topic.
  • Option 2 (ABCD): This starts with the fields' responsibility for fuel production without introducing the context, making it less coherent.
  • Option 4 (BACD): This incorrect sequence places the main introduction (C) after details about the fields, disrupting the logical flow.

questions.question: Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order, except the first part. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. It is… A. who are continually trying to improve B. not the least talented C. their dialogue skills, D. the most talented people
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order, except the first part. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

It is…

A. who are continually trying to improve

B. not the least talented

C. their dialogue skills,

D. the most talented people
questions.solution: The sentence is about talented people and their dialogue skills. The first part of the sentence is missing, so we need to start with the part that makes sense: "It is." So, the first part is D. The next logical part is "not the least talented", which sets up a comparison. So, the next part is A. The third part should be the one that contrasts with "not the least talented", which is "the most talented people". So, C must follow A. Finally, we need to add the part that explains what the most talented people are doing, which is "who are continually trying to improve their dialogue skills". So, the last part is B.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in the correct order. There are P. reports that toy shops and other Q. to prepare for the Christmas rush R. non-food retailers are struggling to S. get enough stock into their warehouses
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in the correct order.

There are

P. reports that toy shops and other

Q. to prepare for the Christmas rush

R. non-food retailers are struggling to

S. get enough stock into their warehouses
questions.solution: The correct answer is: PRSQ. The sentence begins with "There are" followed by (P) "reports that toy shops and other", which introduces the subject. (R) "non-food retailers are struggling to" logically follows "other" to complete the subject group. (S) "get enough stock into their warehouses" provides the object of the struggle, and (Q) "to prepare for the Christmas rush" concludes the sentence by stating the purpose.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. Research shows P. that medium-skilled employees who work Q. in front of a computer and work beyond R. 4.6 effective hours a day produce smaller S. quantities of output per hour due to fatigue
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Research shows

Q. in front of a computer and work beyond

R. 4.6 effective hours a day produce smaller

S. quantities of output per hour due to fatigue
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. 'PQRS'.

Key Points

  • PQRS: This is the correct order because it maintains the logical flow of the sentence.
  • It starts with the subject of the research - "medium-skilled employees who work" (P), goes on to further describe their working conditions - "in front of a computer and work beyond" (Q), and finally presents the conclusion of the research - "4.6 effective hours a day produce smaller" (R) "quantities of output per hour due to fatigue" (S).
  • The sequence PQRS maintains the coherence and completeness of the idea being expressed.

Therefore, the correct order of sentence is: 'PQRS'.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) once said Q) a wise man R) that action speaks S) louder than words

Q) a wise man
R) that action speaks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence conveys a famous saying about the importance of actions over words.
  • Part Q is the first part as it introduces the subject, "a wise man":
    • "a wise man"
  • Part P follows next to indicate what the wise man did, "once said":
    • "once said"
  • Part R is the third part as it begins the quote, "that action speaks":

  • Part S comes last to complete the quote, "louder than words":
